extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images. The dataset requires models to not just read text but interpret it within the layout/structure of the document.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from UCSF Industry Documents Library and hand-picked from different collections. Questions and answers were collected through a three-stage annotation process using remote workers via a web-based annotation tool. Stage 1: workers created up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image. Stage 2: different workers verified by answering the questions and assigning question types. Stage 3: authors reviewed mismatched answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity were not included in the dataset. Questions where answers from stage 1 and stage 2 did not match were sent for author review and either accepted (with editing if necessary) or ignored.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images from 6,071 industry documents from UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning from 1900 to 2018, primarily from 1960-2000. Documents include typewritten, printed, handwritten and born-digital text from 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical) and various document types (letters, forms, reports, tables, etc.). Priority given to non-binarized images and pages with tables, forms, lists and figures.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from 1900 to 2018, with most from 1960-2000
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process: Stage 1 - workers shown document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs with answers verbatim from document; Stage 2 - different workers verify by answering questions from stage 1 and assign question types, with option to flag inappropriate questions; Stage 3 - authors review questions where stage 1 and stage 2 answers don't match exactly, with editing and accept/ignore options
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification through two-stage annotation where stage 2 workers answer questions independently from stage 1, with exact match comparison between stages. Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity are excluded. Mismatches undergo author review in stage 3.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Two independent annotations per question (stage 1 and stage 2), with potential for multiple ground truth answers per question
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR solution used for generating OCR tokens from document images
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limitations related to image quality due to binarization, and models show large performance gaps compared to human performance (94.36% accuracy), particularly on questions requiring understanding of document structure.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images, specifically for training and evaluating models on extractive question answering tasks. It aims to inspire a 'purpose-driven' approach in document image analysis and recognition research.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions and answers collected through three-stage annotation process with verification and review. Questions flagged for language issues or ambiguity were excluded. Questions where first and second stage answers did not match exactly were sent for third stage review and editing.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Document images were hand-picked from UCSF Industry Documents Library collections. Binarized images were minimized due to poor image quality concerns. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. OCR tokens extracted using commercial OCR application.

name.evidence: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA.

description.evidence: The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images... Answering questions in the new dataset require models not just to read text but interpret it within the layout/structure of the document.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library... rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset... Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: During the second stage, if the worker finds a question inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity, an option to flag the question was provided. Most of the documents are from the 1960-2000 period and they include typewritten, printed, handwritten and born-digital text.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: We made use of documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018... Most of the documents are from the 1960-2000 period

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The annotation process was organized in three stages. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it... The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage... If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage... The third stage review is done by the authors themselves.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage. Here a worker was shown an image and questions defined on it in the first stage (but not the answers from the first stage), and was required to enter answers for the questions... if the worker finds a question inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity, an option to flag the question was provided. Such questions are not included in the dataset. If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: We encouraged the workers to add more than one ground truth answer per question in cases where it is warranted... The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage. Here a worker was shown an image and questions defined on it in the first stage (but not the answers from the first stage), and was required to enter answers for the questions.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: For statistics on OCR tokens, for DocVQA we use OCR tokens generated by a commercial OCR solution.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality. We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA... Although the existing models perform reasonably well on certain types of questions, there is large performance gap compared to human performance (94.36% accuracy). The models need to improve specifically on questions where understanding structure of the document is crucial.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA... This makes VQA on the DocVQA dataset an extractive QA problem similar to extractive QA tasks in NLP... We introduce a new data set and an associated VQA task with the aim to inspire a 'purpose-driven' approach in document image analysis and recognition research.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: During the second stage, if the worker finds a question inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity, an option to flag the question was provided. Such questions are not included in the dataset. If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage. Here questions and answers are editable and the reviewer either accepts the question-answer (after editing if necessary) or ignores it.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset. Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality. We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. We also prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages which only have running text. For measuring human performance, we collect answers for all questions in test split, with help a few volunteers from our institution. In all our experiments including heuristics and trained baselines, OCR tokens we use are extracted using a commercial OCR application.
